newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria to boost natgas output 50 pct by start of '9.
newsitem.headline: Syria to boost natgas output 50 pct by start of '9.

text.p: Syria will increase its natural gas output by over 50 percent from the start of 1997 to around 12.5 million cubic metres per day from an estimated eight mcm/d in 1996, official sources said .
The plan is to increase output capacity to over 16 mcm/d in the year 2000 to cover the increasing need for gas in industrial projects and to generate electricity.
On Thursday three gas plants were opened in mid-Syria with a current capacity of 3.0 mcm/d and design capacity of 4.5 mcm/d.

Oil Minister Mohamed Maher Jamal on Thursday opened this first stage of the project -- to gather, separate and dry the free natural gas in the Ark, Hail and Doubiat fields with a design capacity of 4.5 mcm/d.
The whole project -- the first and second stages -- will produce around six mcm/d, the officials said.
The gas would be used at the Zara power station in west Syria instead of fuel oil to reduce pollution. The resulting surplus fuel would be exported.
In the second stage of the project, Syria will complete the gathering and separation stations and pipelines of the Sukhneh and Najib fields to produce around three mcm/d by the end of 1997.
Syria also plans to increase the production of the Gbeseh gas plant to around 3.0 mcm/d from 1.7 mcm/d at the beginning of 1997.

The plant, whose actual starting capacity will be 2.5 mcm/d, will process the gas produced from nearby fields and send it to the amonia uria fertiliser plant in the city of Homs in west Syria. The gas will also run through the pipelines to feed the Homs refinery.
The pipelines' capacity would be increased to 2.5 mcm/d from 1.5 mcm/d to cover the needs of the town of Zara for clean gas and power generation.
Syria opened the Jafra gas plant in the eastern part near the city of Deir ez-Zor to produce 80,000 cm/d for nearby electricity generation stations.
The station will use the gas accompanying oil in the Jafra and Shamal Atallah fields and the surplus of the I'Ziba field.
Syria is investing around $2.14 billion in projects to double its electricity generation capacity to around 6,770 megawatts in 1998 from some 4,240 megawatts now.
Syria produces around 600,000 barrels of oil a day.
